subtitle: Lesson 14 · Data Protection & Encryption

eyebrow: Attachments live in their own table
code:
Incident record:                       sys_attachment:
- read governed by Incident ACL        - a SEPARATE table
- agent sees fields, updates state     - read/download governed by
                                          its OWN ACL, checked
                                          independently
caption: Record access and attachment access are two separate checks.

code:
Incident record ACL:                    sys_attachment ACL:
- read: incident_agent role             - read: incident_agent role
  (sees fields, updates state)             AND attachment_viewer role

Result: agent works the ticket fully, but cannot
download the one sensitive attached file without the extra role.
caption: Full record access does not have to mean full attachment access.

eyebrow: Export is a separate capability from read
code:
List of 4,000 Incident records:
- Read access in the UI:    open and view each record, one at a time
- Export to CSV/Excel:      requires its OWN export-capable role
                             (not granted automatically by read access)
caption: Reading a list and exporting it are different permissions.

eyebrow: Why one-at-a-time and bulk are different risks
code:
In-UI viewing:                          Bulk export:
- stays inside the platform's           - the data leaves the
  access controls and audit trail         platform's reach entirely
- each view is logged                   - can be emailed, copied,
                                           carried anywhere
caption: Same data, very different blast radius if something goes wrong.
